_readme: Copy this file to databases.json, or just run ./setup.sh (setup.ps1 on Windows)
and it writes both this file and the matching .env entries for you.
Each entry under "profiles" is one database this server can query. Every MCP
tool takes an optional "profile" argument; omit it and "defaultProfile" is
used. The AI discovers what exists by calling the list_databases tool.
A profile is written in ONE of two styles - never both:
A) discrete fields: host, port, database, user, password, ssl
B) a single connection string: url
NEVER put a password or a full URL literally in this file. Use ${VAR} and put
the value in .env. Keeping this file secret-free is what makes it safe to
bind-mount read-only into Docker, readable by the container's non-root user,
and safe to paste into a bug report. Write $${VAR} for a literal ${VAR}.
Profile names: lowercase letters, digits and underscore, starting with a
letter, max 32 chars. Reserved: all, default, none, profiles, list.
Keys starting with _ (like this one) and $schema are ignored by the server,
so you can leave notes here. Everything else must be a key the server knows -
a typo like "hosts" is reported as an error rather than silently ignored.

neon._comment: Style A - discrete fields. Use when you know host/database/user.

local._comment: Style B - one URL. Use when your provider handed you a connection string.
